newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala, El Salvador sign free trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala, El Salvador sign free trade agreement.

text.p: Guatemala and El Salvador signed Thursday morning an agreement to establish free trade between the two countries next year, said a government official.

"The two presidents are signing a declaration that we will start to work on the process that will take us to implenting a customs union. That is something that has to happen in 1997," said Guatemala's Economy Minister Juan Mauricio Wurmser.
Armando Calderon Sol, the president of El Salvador, is visiting Guatemala, where he attended Wednesday's summit of Central American heads of state with South Korea's President Kim Young-sam.

Wurmser said Guatemala and El Salvador will eliminate duties between the two countries and establish a common tariff structure for external trade, as well as common customs policies and health and sanitary requirements for imports.

Wurmser said the combined production of Guatemala and El Salvador is equal to 53 percent of the gross product of the region. According to the minister, eliminating tariffs between the two countries would strengthen initiatives for free trade with other countries and efforts towards Central American integration.
